Google has quietly dropped what researchers are calling "Attention Is All You Need V2."

And it signals the end of the Transformer era as we know it.

In 2017, the original "Attention Is All You Need" paper changed the world by proving that AI doesn't need recurrence, it just needs to pay attention.

But today, even the most advanced models like GPT and Gemini suffer from a massive, structural flaw: Catastrophic Forgetting.

The moment an AI learns something new, it starts losing what it learned before. It’s why AI "hallucinates" or loses the thread in long conversations.

This paper, titled "Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architectures," completely replaces the way AI stores information.

The researchers have introduced a paradigm shift called Nested Learning (NL).

Here is why this is "V2":

For the last decade, we treated AI models as one giant, flat mathematical function. NL proves that a model is actually a set of thousands of smaller, "nested" optimization problems running in parallel.

Instead of one giant "memory," each layer has its own internal "context flow." This allows the model to learn new tasks at test-time without overwriting its core intelligence.

It moves us past the static Transformer. The new architecture (HOPE) demonstrated 100% stability in long-context memory and "post-training adaptation" that was previously impossible.

The technical takeaway is brutal for the competition:

Existing deep learning works by compressing information until it breaks. Nested Learning works by organizing information so it can grow forever.

We’ve spent 7 years trying to make Transformers bigger. Google figured out how to make them "Nested."

The Transformer replaced the RNN in 2017.

Nested Learning is here to replace the Transformer in 2026.

1924 年，丹麦比隆，一个木匠的车间烧成了灰。

他叫 Ole Kirk Christiansen，33 岁。

他从很小就在做木工。在比隆开了自己的工坊，做门、做窗、做家具、做农具。

这场火是他两个儿子玩木屑引起的。

车间没了，工具没了，库存的木材也没了。

他借钱重新开张。

1929 年，全球进入大萧条。

丹麦农民买不起家具，他的订单一夜之间消失。

他坐在空荡的工坊里做了一个决定——既然没人买大件，他改做小件。

他开始做玩具。

木头做的鸭子、卡车、小车。

周围的人说："家里都快吃不上饭了，你做这种东西？"

Christiansen 说："这种东西能让孩子记一辈子。"

他把丹麦语 "Leg godt"（玩得好）的前两个音节缩成一个词，给自己的小作坊起名：LEGO。

那是 1934 年。

1942 年，他的车间又烧了。

这一次损失比第一次更大——库存、模具、设计图全部化灰。

他又重建了一次。

1947 年，他做了一件 50 多岁的木匠不该做的事——他借钱买了一台塑料注塑机。

整个丹麦的玩具行业都在嘲笑：一个木匠去做塑料？

1949 年，他做出了第一批可以互相咬合的塑料积木。

粗糙，松，孩子拼一会儿就散。

但他没停。

他和他的儿子改良了将近十年。

1958 年专利下来——那个有圆点、有底管、可以严丝合缝拼无限种东西的积木，终于成型了。

专利下来同一年，Christiansen 死了。

他没看到 LEGO 后来怎么变成世界上最大的玩具公司。

也没看到 1960 年的第三场火——他剩下的木质玩具仓库烧了。

他的儿子 Godtfred 做了最后一个决定：不再做木头玩具了。

LEGO 的木质时代结束，塑料时代开始。

还记得上次 Claude 停掉了 Claude Code 订阅在 OpenClaw 的调用吗？甚至连 claude -p 这种调用都限制了，不能再共享 Claude 订阅。

但当还留了个口子，就是基于 Claude Agent SDK 和 claude -p 还是能跑能共享订阅额度的。

现在他们有一个新的方案，把这个口子也堵上了。美名其曰给你额外额度用于程序化调用，也就是 Agent SDK、claude -p 命令行、Claude Code GitHub Actions、以及 Conductor 和 OpenClaw 这类基于 Agent SDK 的第三方工具。

但实际上额度小的可怜，Pro 20 美元，Max 5x 100 美元，Max 20x 200 美元，Team 标准席位 20 美元一人，Team 高级席位 100 美元一人。

按 Anthropic 自己的 API 价格算，Pro 的 20 美元用 Sonnet 只够大约六七百万 token 输入或一百多万 token 输出，几轮密集的 agent 循环就见底。Max 20x 用户每月付 200 美元订阅费，拿到的 SDK credit 正好也是 200 美元。

关键在于变化方向。之前 SDK 和交互式聊天共用订阅套餐的 rate limit（速率限制），Claude Code 重度用户能在订阅价格下跑出远超 200 美元等价的 API 用量，这是订阅模式的吸引力所在。现在 SDK 端被按美元封顶，相当于把这块超额价值收回去了。Anthropic 在帮助文档里也挑明：团队跑生产级共享自动化的，应该转去 Claude Developer Platform 用 API key 按量付费，订阅套餐"不是为这个场景设计的"。

受冲击最大的是第三方工具用户。之前用 OpenClaw、Conductor 这类基于 Agent SDK 的 agent 工具的人，本质上是"用订阅价跑高频自动化"。新政之下，这条路只剩 credit 那一点点额度可走，烧完要么转 extra usage（额外用量，按 API 价付钱）继续跑，要么停到下个月 credit 重置。

不受影响的部分：API key 用户照旧按量付费；交互式 Claude Code（终端和 IDE 里手敲那种）、Claude Cowork，以及网页/桌面/手机端的 Claude 聊天，都继续走原本的订阅限额。

6 月 8 日 Anthropic 会给符合条件的用户发邮件领取，6 月 15 日生效。

然后转身跑了。

后来跟小区保安聊，说这小孩是隔壁楼的，爸妈做生意的，根本不差钱。

她就是喜欢玩找人借钱再找零的游戏，

她每次都真的凑整找零，让你完全不起疑心。

我花一百块，买了个道理：

不要小看任何人的专业技能。六岁的小孩，骗起人来比你会计都严谨。

RCA was the original AI stock. 

On July 1, 1920, at the explicit request of the United States Navy, four corporations signed a cross-licensing agreement that pooled every significant radio patent in American hands: General Electric (which had absorbed American Marconi at the Navy's direction), Westinghouse Electric, the American Telephone and Telegraph Company, and the United Fruit Company.

The last name on the list is the unexpected one. United Fruit had developed a patent on a tropical-band radio system used to coordinate banana shipping fleets between Central America and New Orleans. That patent turned out to cover techniques essential to commercial broadcasting.

The underlying technology that made the radio possible — the vacuum-tube amplifier, the continuous-wave transmitter, the superheterodyne receiver — was developed at General Electric, Westinghouse, and AT&T over the previous fifteen years.

The entity that would manufacture sets, operate stations, and sell broadcast time was the newly created Radio Corporation of America. GE owned 30 percent. Westinghouse owned 21 percent. AT&T owned 10 percent. United Fruit owned 4 percent. Owen D. Young, vice president of General Electric, was its chairman. James Harbord, a retired Army major general, was its president.

On the night of July 2, 1921, Jack Dempsey knocked out the French light-heavyweight champion Georges Carpentier in the fourth round of a heavyweight title fight at Boyle's Thirty Acres, an outdoor arena in Jersey City, New Jersey. The official paid attendance was 80,183 — the largest gate in boxing history to that point. But three hundred thousand people heard the fight live – via the radio.

They sat in their homes and listened to a transmission broadcast from a temporary 1.5-kilowatt station operating under the call sign WJY, set up nine days earlier in a shed in Hoboken by RCA’s 30-year-old commercial manager, David Sarnoff. The signal was also carried by wire to amplifier shacks in eight cities, where it was rebroadcast to crowds gathered in armory halls, hotel ballrooms, and theaters from Boston to Pittsburgh.

In the 1920s, broadcast infrastructure grew on a trajectory no industry had ever matched.
In December 1921, the U.S. Commerce Department recognized 29 licensed broadcasting stations. By September 1922, the count reached 510. By October 5, 1922 — ten months later — there were 546. 

The hardware to receive the signal kept pace with the growth in stations. American radio set sales went from $60 million in 1922 to $358 million in 1924 to $650 million in 1928. 

By 1929 the United States manufactured 4.4 million radio receivers — one for every six American households — generating $843 million in factory wholesale revenue, a fourteen-fold expansion in seven years.
Vacuum tube production — the core component, the equivalent of the GPU in today's AI build-out —were dominated by RCA's Harrison, New Jersey plant, by Westinghouse's East Pittsburgh works, and by GE's Schenectady operation. Together those three facilities produced more than 80 percent of all licensed vacuum tubes manufactured in the United States during the 1920s, employing approximately 12,000 workers at peak.

On September 9, 1926, RCA created the National Broadcasting Company — two networks, 24 affiliate stations linked by AT&T telephone lines, programming syndicated from a single master control room in New York. In 1928, the Columbia Broadcasting System launched in competition with 16 affiliate stations. By 1929, NBC had absorbed approximately 100 affiliates across its Red and Blue networks. Advertising revenue — a category that had not existed in 1921 — reached $40 million in 1929.

In January 1929, RCA acquired the Victor Talking Machine Company, the largest manufacturer of phonograph records and home phonographs in the world, for $154 million in stock. The acquisition turned RCA from a radio set manufacturer dependent on Westinghouse and GE production into a vertically integrated entertainment conglomerate that wrote the programs, made the records, broadcast the signal, sold the receiver, and collected royalties on every patent involved at every step. RCA was added to the Dow Jones Industrial Average on October 1, 1928.

Eight years after Dempsey-Carpentier, RCA was the most heavily traded stock in the United States. It generated $182 million in gross income from radio set sales, broadcast advertising, music records, and patent royalties. RCA dividends totaled $5 per share. And, at its high, the stock traded at $114.75, after a 5-for-1 split. The pre-split equivalent was $568. The 1922 starting price had been $1.50.

About a month after RCA made its all-time high, on Monday, October 28, the Dow fell 13 percent. On Tuesday, October 29 the Dow fell another 12 percent. By the end of two trading days, the index had lost 23 percent of its value. By November 13, the Dow stood at 198.69, down 48 percent from the September peak. The decline did not stop in November. It continued for thirty-two more months. The Dow reached its trough on July 8, 1932, at 41.22 — down 89.2 percent from the September 3, 1929, peak.

RCA traded that day at $2.625, down 98 percent. 

Nothing had changed about the technology or its incredible value to Americans. By 1940, there were 765 licensed broadcasting stations operating in the United States, reaching 28 million American homes with radio receivers. 

RCA thrived. David Sarnoff became its third president on January 3, 1930, three months after the crash, and ran the company for the next 41 years.

Timeline of Tokens on Bitcoin: 14+ Years of History

2012-03-27  Colored Coins concept
Yoni Assia (later CEO of eToro) publishes “Bitcoin 2.X.”
One of the first proposals to tag individual satoshis with metadata.
Vitalik Buterin later contributed to Colored Coins discussions before eventually building Ethereum.

2012-12-04  Colored Coins whitepaper
Meni Rosenfeld formalizes the specification.
Defines genesis transactions and color tracking rules.
Influences later Bitcoin tokenization experiments and eventually ideas that inspired ERC-20 assets.

Cycle 1: Tokens and NFTs on Bitcoin

2013-07-31  Mastercoin / Omni Protocol
JR Willett publishes “The Second Bitcoin Whitepaper.”
Raises ~5,000 BTC in one of crypto’s first ICOs.
Later becomes Omni Layer and eventually hosts Tether.

2013-12-01  Open Assets Protocol
Flavien Charlon ships an early colored coin implementation.
Uses OP_RETURN for asset tracking.
One of the first practical colored coin systems on Bitcoin.

2014-01-15  Counterparty (XCP)
2,140 BTC burned to mint XCP.
One of the first Bitcoin protocols with native assets, a DEX, and smart contract style functionality.
Still active more than a decade later.

2014-10-06  Tether launches on Omni
Originally launched as “Realcoin” before rebranding to Tether later in 2014.
The first major stablecoin launched on Bitcoin through Omni Layer.

2015-03-21  Spells of Genesis
Blockchain trading card game built on Counterparty.
Predates Ethereum and CryptoKitties.
Considered one of the earliest NFTs.

2016-09-09  Rare Pepes
First Rare Pepe card minted at Bitcoin block 428,919.
Predates the term “NFT” and projects like CryptoPunks.
Helped establish early Bitcoin collectible culture.

2017-08-24  SegWit activates
Segregated Witness soft fork activates.
Fixes transaction malleability and discounts witness data.
Creates the foundation later used by Ordinals and inscriptions.

2018-01-04  Rootstock (RSK)
RSK mainnet launches.
Merge mined Bitcoin sidechain with EVM compatibility.
Enables smart contracts secured by Bitcoin miners.

2018-03-15  Lightning Network mainnet era begins
Lightning Labs releases lnd 0.4 for Bitcoin mainnet.
Payment channels enable fast and cheap Bitcoin payments.
Later becomes important infrastructure for Taproot Assets.

2018-09-27  Liquid Network
Blockstream launches Liquid.
Federated Bitcoin sidechain with issued assets and confidential transactions.
Used heavily by exchanges and trading desks.

2019-02-08  Tether expands beyond Bitcoin
USDT issuance expands aggressively onto Ethereum and Tron.
Omni usage gradually declines as liquidity migrates to other chains.

2020-08-11  MicroStrategy buys Bitcoin
Michael Saylor announces MicroStrategy’s first major BTC purchase.
Helps kick off the corporate Bitcoin treasury era.

2021-01-14  Stacks 2.0 mainnet
Stacks launches Proof of Transfer.
Smart contract chain anchored to Bitcoin.
Introduces Clarity smart contracts.

2021-11-14  Taproot activates
Taproot soft fork activates at block 709,632.
Introduces Schnorr signatures and script tree commitments.
Creates the infrastructure later used by inscription envelopes.

2022-12-14  First Ordinal inscription
Casey Rodarmor creates inscription 0 at block 767,430.
First widely recognized inscription embedded directly into a satoshi.

Cycle 2: Inscriptions, NFTs, and fungible tokens

2023-01-21  Ordinals launches
Casey Rodarmor releases ord v0.1.
Introduces sat numbering and inscription indexing.
Turns individual sats into uniquely traceable digital artifacts.

2023-03-08  BRC-20 launches
Domo publishes the BRC-20 experiment.
Simple JSON based fungible token standard using inscriptions.
At peak periods in 2023, BRC-20 related activity represented over half of Bitcoin transactions.

2023-04-15  Bitcoin Stamps (SRC-20)
Mike In Space launches Stamps.
Stores image data directly in spendable outputs.
Markets itself as highly permanent Bitcoin art storage.

2023-04-26  RGB protocol mainnet
RGB client side validation system launches.
Concept originally proposed years earlier.
Designed for scalable assets on Bitcoin and Lightning.

2023-06-05  Recursive inscriptions
ord v0.8 introduces recursive inscription support.
Inscriptions can reference other inscriptions.
Enables fully onchain generative art, games, and applications.
OCM Dimensions is one of the landmark examples.

2023-09-07  TAP protocol
BennyTheDev and the Trac ecosystem introduce TAP.
A more programmable evolution of BRC-20 with authorities, whitelist mints, redemptions, mass send, and Digital Matter Theory assets.
One of the first major attempts to push Bitcoin fungible tokens beyond simple JSON minting.

2023-09-22  Atomicals (ARC-20)
Atomicals Protocol launches.
Introduces UTXO native token ideas and Realm names.
Alternative approach to fungible tokens before Runes.

2023-10-09  BitVM paper
Robin Linus publishes the BitVM paper.
Proposes optimistic computation and Bitcoin verification schemes without requiring a soft fork.

2023-10-18  Taproot Assets
Lightning Labs launches Taproot Assets.
Bitcoin native asset protocol designed for Lightning integration.
Focused heavily on stablecoin and institutional payment use cases.

2023-12-15  PIPE protocol
Trac ecosystem launches PIPE.
UTXO-native fungible token design focused on reducing indexer complexity and improving scalability versus BRC-20.
Part of a broader push toward a Bitcoin-native OrdFi stack.

2023-12-17  Runestone airdrop
Leonidas distributes Runestone inscriptions.
One of the largest Bitcoin inscription airdrops.
Helps reignite Ordinals ecosystem activity.

2024-01-10  Spot Bitcoin ETFs approved
US regulators approve spot Bitcoin ETFs including BlackRock’s IBIT.
Massive institutional inflows reshape Bitcoin market structure.

2024-04-20  Runes activates
Casey Rodarmor launches Runes at the fourth Bitcoin halving.
UTXO native fungible token protocol built directly around Bitcoin transaction structure.

2024-05-01  Counterparty modernization
Counterparty ecosystem ships major modernization upgrades.
A reminder that one of Bitcoin’s earliest token protocols is still alive.

2024-08-22  Babylon Bitcoin staking
Babylon launches Bitcoin staking.
Allows BTC to help secure external systems without traditional bridging.

2024-08-26  Alkanes
Experimental smart contract layer associated with the Runes ecosystem.
Explores WASM style programmability for Bitcoin native assets.

2024-09-09  Fractal Bitcoin
UniSat launches Fractal Bitcoin.
Merge mined Bitcoin compatible sidechain with faster blocks.
Supports Bitcoin native asset experimentation.

2024-10-29  Stacks Nakamoto and sBTC
Stacks ships the Nakamoto upgrade.
sBTC launches later with a Bitcoin pegged asset model.
Major step toward a more active Bitcoin anchored smart contract economy.

2026-05-12  This week
Fungible token related activity represents a major share of Bitcoin transactions.
Bitcoin tokenization and asset issuance continue evolving more than 14 years after Colored Coins.

New statements from Windward indicates that Iran still has about 23 days (at least) of on-vessel storage capacity until they hit tank tops. Combined with recent satellite imagery published by TankerTrackers showing available remaining storage on Kharg, Iran likely has ~30 days in total between onshore and on-vessel storage before approaching full capacity. 

Taking into account other measures Iran has taken to extend this timeline, including trucking routes into Pakistan, rail lines into China, and likely smuggling into Iraq, it is fair to assess that Iran has (at least) 35 days remaining. Utilizing historical “extreme measures” as a reference, where Saddam Hussein intentionally dumped around 10M barrels into the Gulf in the 1990’s, this would further add another 10 days to the timeline alone. To be clear… I do not advocate for such measures, but I’m operating in reality where if Iran truly risks “catastrophic” long-term damage, they would take emergency measures such as this to extend that timeline.

Best case scenario: ~35-45 days remaining. 

This is significant for a few reasons: 

1) Particularly egregious reporting from Fox News insinuated that Iran was intentionally dumping oil into the Gulf based on the satellite imagery of an oil slick near Kharg. There is conflicting reporting around the volume of this slick, with NYT stating 3,000 barrels, and other sources indicating 70,000 barrels. While this is not “environmentally” great, if Iran resorts to intentional dumping of oil into the Gulf, it’ll be measured in the millions of barrels… not the thousands. 

2) Satellite imagery shows the Iran has not loaded any oil onto vessels at Kharg over the past few days. Some have extrapolated this to conclude Iran has reached tank tops. Obviously, as can be derived from the statements made today by Windward, this is obviously not true. Iran has (at least) 23 days of available on-vessel storage remaining.
